__comment: second-opinion monitoring dashboard. Import via Grafana → Dashboards → Import, then pick your Loki data source. Expects the reviewer's Loki events (set LOKI_URL / loki-url; see README 'Monitoring'). Works against Grafana Cloud Loki and self-hosted Loki alike. The Tempo data source is optional and only powers the trace links in the two tables — leave it unset unless you also run tracing (otlp-endpoint).
title: second-opinion

list.__comment: Only the trace links use this. Tracing is opt-in (otlp-endpoint), so leave it unset if you don't run it — every panel here queries Loki and works regardless. A datasource variable rather than a hardcoded uid because Tempo uids differ per stack.
list.name: tempo
list.label: Tempo data source (for trace links)

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", outcome="posted", repo=~"${repo:regex}"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Degraded / errored
panels.description: Reviews that posted nothing (or errored). This is the reviewer-malfunction rate — the runtime counterpart of the fail-on-degraded tripwire.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", outcome=~"degraded|error", repo=~"${repo:regex}"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Review spend
panels.description: Sum of per-review cost estimates (list-price based for agentic passes, so treat as ≈).

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap cost_usd | __error__="" [$__range]))
sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap tokens | __error__="" [$__range]))

panels.__comment: Added 2026-08-22 after a $7.80 review night read as 'the model got more expensive'. It hadn't: these separate the RATE from the VOLUME, which the spend panels above deliberately pool (they answer 'what did today cost', not 'why'). A flat rate under a rising bill means more reviews or bigger diffs.
panels.title: Unit economics — rate, not volume

panels.__comment: The headline 'did the price go up' panel, and the one most likely to be misread on its own — which is why the token-mix row below exists.
panels.description: Blended USD per million tokens billed. NOT the list price: `tokens` pools four classes that bill an order of magnitude apart ($0.08 fresh input, $0.18 output, $0.016 cache read per Mtok on deepseek-v4-flash-0731), so this line moves with the MIX as much as with the price. Read it next to 'Cache hit rate' — if the mix holds steady and this moves, that is a genuine reprice and nothing else it could be. Sawtooth with a moving hit rate is just caching.

targets.expr: 1e6 * sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap cost_usd | __error__="" [$__auto])) / sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap tokens | __error__="" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Effective rate ($ / Mtok)

panels.__comment: Mean not median: the tail IS the bill, and a p50 would hide the 12-round PR that dominated the night of 2026-08-21.
panels.description: Mean USD per review event, degraded runs included (they cost real money and excluding them flatters the average). Rises when diffs get bigger or K goes up — not when the model repriced.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap cost_usd | __error__="" [$__auto])) / sum(count_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"}[$__auto]))

panels.title: Cost per review (mean)

panels.description: Mean tokens per review — the volume half of cost per review. cost/review = tokens/review x rate, so any two of these three panels explain the third.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap tokens | __error__="" [$__auto])) / sum(count_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"}[$__auto]))

panels.title: Tokens per review (mean)

panels.__comment: The one to trust when the bill jumps. Volume-invariant by construction.
panels.description: USD per 100k characters of diff reviewed — cost normalised by the work actually asked for, and the fairest 'are reviews getting dearer' signal here. Posted reviews only: a degraded run has no diff_chars to divide by. A busy day of large PRs leaves it flat; more retries or worse caching raise it.

targets.expr: 1e5 * sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", outcome="posted", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap cost_usd | __error__="" [$__auto])) / sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", outcome="posted", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap diff_chars | __error__="" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Cost per 100k diff chars

panels.__comment: The attribution layer for the rate panel above. Needs the token split (tokens_input/output/cache_read/cache_write), added to the review, pass and merge events in the same change; these panels are empty for any review logged before that shipped, which is expected and not a broken query.
panels.title: Token mix — where the money actually goes

panels.__comment: The panel this whole row was built for. Ratio against `tokens` deliberately — the four classes are not a partition and must not be summed to form a denominator (see _token_split_fields in run.py).
panels.description: tokens_cache_read / tokens — the cached share of the BILLED TOTAL. Deliberately not cache_read / (cache_read + input), which answers a different question and is not comparable with the cost panels beside it. Usually the biggest single lever on this bill: cache reads cost 1/5 of fresh input and 1/11 of output, so hits falling from 90% to 50% roughly triples spend with the list price untouched. A drop here explains a rising effective rate; a steady line means the rate moved for some other reason. Above 100% would mean the provider reports a cache-EXCLUSIVE total — not clamped, so that stays visible rather than hidden.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} |= "tokens_cache_read" | json | unwrap tokens_cache_read | __error__="" [$__auto])) / sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} |= "tokens_cache_read" | json | unwrap tokens | __error__="" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Cache hit rate

panels.__comment: Ordered cache read / input / output so the stack reads cheap-to-dear bottom-up and a widening top band is visibly the expensive one.
panels.description: The four classes as reported, stacked. Cheapest at the bottom, so a healthy review is mostly the bottom band and a widening top band is the expensive one. Bands do not double-count for pi, which reports the four disjointly (verified: totalTokens == input+output+cacheRead+cacheWrite on every real record); a provider that folded cached tokens into its input count would show them in two bands at once. Note the stack totals every review in each bucket, so its height is not any one review's `tokens` — compare against the Tokens-by-repo panel for the same window rather than reading a per-review figure off this one.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} |= "tokens_cache_read" | json | unwrap tokens_cache_read | __error__="" [$__auto]))
sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} |= "tokens_cache_read" | json | unwrap tokens_input | __error__="" [$__auto]))
sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} |= "tokens_cache_read" | json | unwrap tokens_output | __error__="" [$__auto]))
sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} |= "tokens_cache_read" | json | unwrap tokens_cache_write | __error__="" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Token mix

panels.__comment: The other half of the mix story: cache hit rate explains the cheap end, this explains the dear end.
panels.description: Output's share of billed tokens. Output is the dearest class at $0.18/Mtok — 11x a cache read — so a small rise here moves the effective rate more than its size suggests. Climbs when the model reasons or writes more per review, which is a prompt/model change, not a price change.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} |= "tokens_cache_read" | json | unwrap tokens_output | __error__="" [$__auto])) / sum(sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} |= "tokens_cache_read" | json | unwrap tokens | __error__="" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Output share

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (count_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"}[$__auto]))
sum by (repo) (sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap cost_usd | __error__="" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Review duration
panels.description: Wall-clock per review (all K passes + merge + post).

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.50, {service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap duration_s | __error__="" [$__auto]) by ()
quantile_over_time(0.95, {service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap duration_s | __error__="" [$__auto]) by ()
sum by (repo) (sum_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap tokens | __error__="" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Review rounds per PR
panels.description: How many second-opinion reviews each PR has accumulated in the selected range (a force-push mints a new head SHA and earns a fresh round). Counts posted reviews only — skipped/degraded attempts are not rounds.

targets.expr: topk(25, sum by (repo, pr) (count_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", outcome="posted", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json [$__range])))

panels.title: Sweeps (daemon liveness)
panels.description: One event per daemon sweep (delivery=daemon only — Action runs also emit sweep events, and unscoped they would paper over a real gap in the daemon's cadence). A gap here means the daemon is down or wedged. Outcomes: ok = healthy sweep; silent_failure = sweep ran but ≥1 review degraded/errored with nothing posted; skipped = local llama-server unreachable; error = sweeps running but throwing before completing.

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (count_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="sweep", delivery="daemon", repo=~"${repo:regex}"}[$__auto]))

panels.title: Degraded passes — what they burned
panels.description: Every pass that did NOT end 'ok', ranked by tokens spent before it stopped. The review event pools spend across all K passes, so it cannot distinguish a pass that died instantly from one that burned millions first (the runaway signature: 12.6M tokens, $1.96, zero output). A large number here with status=timeout is the case for max-pass-tokens; a small one means the pass failed early and a spend ceiling would not have helped. Click the trace id to see WHERE it stopped — the tokens say how much it burned, the waterfall says on which turn. Blank trace column = tracing was off for that repo.

targets.expr: topk(25, sum by (repo, pr, pass, status, trace_id) (max_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="pass", outcome!="ok", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap tokens | __error__="" [$__range])))

panels.title: Pass duration
panels.description: Wall-clock per agentic pass. Read against 'Review duration': that panel also includes diff fetch, worktree setup, merge and post, so the gap between the two is harness overhead rather than model time. Watch for a rising curve — a pass timeout is usually the end of a latency creep, not a sudden hang.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.50, {service="second-opinion", event="pass", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap elapsed_s | __error__="" [$__auto]) by ()
quantile_over_time(0.95, {service="second-opinion", event="pass", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | unwrap elapsed_s | __error__="" [$__auto]) by ()

panels.title: Union merge health (K>1)
panels.description: The K>1 editorial merge. merged = first attempt worked; merged_on_retry = attempt 1 failed and the retry saved it; fallback = both failed and the raw passes were posted unmerged. Only 'fallback' annotates in CI, so merged_on_retry appearing at all is the early warning — it is the same failure, one attempt short of costing you the union. A sustained run of either is usually the provider, not chance: a 402 followed by an empty 200 is credits exhaustion, which recurs every sweep until fixed (check the 'failures' field in the forensics panel).

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (count_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="merge", repo=~"${repo:regex}"}[$__auto]))

panels.title: Slowest reviews — click a trace id for the waterfall
panels.description: The way in to a single review's shape. The events tell you a review took 726s; the trace tells you where the 726s went — which pass, which model turn, how many output tokens it was emitting at the time. Ranked slowest first, because that is the review worth opening. Empty unless tracing is on (otlp-endpoint): the trace id is the join key between these events and Tempo, and it is only emitted when a trace was actually exported, so a row here always has a trace behind it. Links need the Tempo data source variable set at the top.

targets.expr: topk(25, sum by (repo, pr, outcome, trace_id) (max_over_time({service="second-opinion", event="review", repo=~"${repo:regex}"} | json | trace_id != "" | unwrap duration_s | __error__="" [$__range])))

defaults.noValue: No traced reviews in this range. Tracing is opt-in — set otlp-endpoint (see README 'Tracing').

targets.expr: {service="second-opinion", repo=~"${repo:regex}"}
